nodes.name: NF Cleaning
nodes.procedure: The nickel foam (2 × 3 cm²) was cleaned consecutively by 1.5 M hydrochloric acid, acetone, and ethanol for 15 min, and then stored in ethanol for later use.

nodes.name: Hydrothermal Growth
nodes.procedure: 2 mmol Ni(NO3)2·6H2O and 2 mmol Na2MoO4·2H2O were dissolved in 40 mL of water, and then transferred into a 50 mL Teflon-lined stainless steel autoclave. The cleaned NF was immersed into the solution and placed against the wall of autoclave. Subsequently, the autoclave was maintained at 150°C for 6 h. The NF was taken out and cleaned by sonication several times to obtain the precursor, which was labeled as Ni-Mo-O/NF.

nodes.characterization_summary: XRD pattern of Ni-MoO2/NF reveals diffraction peaks of cubic Ni (PDF #04-0850). NiMoO4/NF shows crystalline NiMoO4 species (PDF #86-0361).
nodes.evidence_snippet: the diffraction peaks in the XRD pattern (Figure 1b) reveal the presence of cubic Ni (PDF # 04-0850). When replacing H2/Ar by pure Ar, the crystalline NiMoO4 species (PDF # 86-0361) are obtained...

nodes.characterization_summary: SEM images show uniform nanorods of Ni-Mo-O/NF well-aligned on nickel foam becoming rough and curving after pyrolysis for Ni-MoO2/NF.
nodes.evidence_snippet: It is seen from the SEM images (Figure S1a,b, Supporting Information) that the uniform nanorods of Ni-Mo-O/NF are well-aligned on the nickel foam... the smooth surfaces of Ni-Mo-O nanorods become rough and curving after pyrolysis under H2/Ar atmosphere (Figure 1c,d).

nodes.characterization_summary: TEM reveals ultrafine Ni nanoparticles on MoO2 nanorod surface with intimate heterointerfaces in Ni-MoO2/NF.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The TEM image (Figure 1e) of Ni - MoO2 / NF reveals the ultrafine nanoparticles form in situ on the nanorod surface to obtain the intimate heterointerfaces.

nodes.characterization_summary: HRTEM shows lattice fringes of 0.203 nm for Ni (111) plane and amorphous MoO2 substrate in Ni-MoO2/NF.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The high-resolution TEM image (Figure 1f) of Ni - MoO2 / NF displays the well-resolved lattice fringes with the interplanar spacing of 0.203nm for nanoparticles, corresponding to (111) plane of cubic-phase Ni, while the adjacent nanorod substrate shows the amorphous feature.

nodes.characterization_summary: SAED pattern shows typical diffraction rings ascribed to metallic Ni for Ni-MoO2/NF.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Specially, only the typical diffraction rings ascribed to metallic Ni are observed on the SAED pattern of Ni - MoO2 / NF in Figure 1g.

nodes.characterization_summary: STEM HAADF/BF images reveal ultrasmall Ni nanoparticles adhering firmly to MoO2 nanorods.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Furthermore, the STEM associated with HAADF/BF-STEM images in Figure 1h again reveal the ultrasmall nanoparticles adhere firmly to the surface of nanorods.

nodes.characterization_summary: EDX elemental mapping shows Ni nanoparticles intimately dispersed on Mo nanorods with homogeneous O distribution.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Elemental mapping under EDX in Figure 1i exhibits the Ni element-composed nanoparticles intimately disperse on Mo element-composed nanorods. And the O element also exhibits the homogeneous distribution on nanorods.

nodes.characterization_summary: XPS Ni 2p shows peaks at 852.7 eV (Ni⁰) and 856.3 eV (Ni²⁺) with shift to higher energies vs pristine Ni; Mo 3d at 229.8/232.5 eV (Mo⁴⁺) shifted lower vs MoO₂; O 1s oxygen vacancy at 531.4 eV in Ni-MoO₂ interfaces.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The peak at about 852.7eV in Ni 2p3/2 region (Figure 2a) is assigned to Ni⁰, and the pronounced subpeak located at 856.3eV and its satellite peak at 862.1eV indicate the high-valence Ni²⁺... For Mo 3d region (Figure 2b), the peaks located at 229.8 and 232.5eV are assigned to Mo⁴⁺... The fitted peaks in Mo 3d region corresponded to Ni - MoO₂ are shifted to lower energies relative to those of MoO₂... the peaks at 852.7 and 869.9eV in Ni 2p region assignable to metallic Ni are shifted to higher energies compared with pristine Ni sample... The peak centered at 531.4eV is related to oxygen vacancy in Ni - MoO₂ heterointerfaces, whilst this peak is absent in MoO₂ sample.

nodes.characterization_summary: Valence band maximum shifts from 0.63 eV (pristine Ni) to 1.51 eV (Ni-MoO2), indicating d-band center shift.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The maximum value of valence band is calculated to be about 0.63 and 1.51eV for pristine Ni and Ni - MoO2 heterostructure, respectively.

nodes.characterization_summary: Ni-MoO₂/NF shows higher C_dl (electrochemical double layer capacitance) than Ni/NF, NiMoO₄/NF, and MoO₂/NF, indicating larger electrochemically active surface area.
nodes.evidence_snippet: We further measured their respective electrochemically active surface area (ECSA) by measuring the electrochemical double layer capacitance (C_dl)... the calculated C_dl of Ni - MoO₂ / NF (Figure S8, Supporting Information) is still much higher than other prepared samples.
